item.title: Autumn events programme announced for King’s Lynn and West Norfolk
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Autumn events programme announced for King’s Lynn and West Norfolk
A variety of cultural events are scheduled across King’s Lynn and West Norfolk this autumn. The King’s Lynn Festival has announced its new season, featuring coffee concerts and talks, while the West Norfolk Wyrdfest runs from October 8 to November 6 at various venues.
Local museums are also hosting activities, with weekly lunchtime talks at True’s Yard and coffee mornings at Lynn Museum. Music fans can look forward to organ recitals at Lynn Minster, performances at the Hunstanton Bandstand, and a tribute to Whitney Houston. Additionally, the KLODS production of The Addams Family Musical takes place from October 29 to 31 at the Peter Hopkins Hall. Residents are encouraged to check venue websites for ticket availability and further information.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Nominations open for 2027 King’s Lynn and West Norfolk Mayor’s Business Awards
Nominations are now open for the 38th annual Mayor’s Business Awards, which celebrate excellence across West Norfolk. Businesses are invited to put forward candidates for 11 categories, including the Apprentice and Trainee of the Year award, sponsored by Whitings Group. This specific category is open to individuals aged 35 or under who have demonstrated exceptional workplace contributions.
The awards ceremony will take place on Friday, March 5, 2027, at the Alive Corn Exchange in King’s Lynn. Organised by the Lynn News and Your Local Paper, the event highlights the achievements of the local business community. Interested parties have until 5pm on Friday, November 27, to submit their nominations. Further details are available through the event organisers.

item.title: Quarter-century milestone for King’s Lynn hospital radio presenter
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Quarter-century milestone for King’s Lynn hospital radio presenter
A long-serving presenter at Hospital Radio Lynn has marked 25 years of broadcasting. Mike Wing was joined by colleagues and former volunteers on Friday, September 18, to celebrate his quarter-century of service at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital.
During his time at the station, Mr. Wing has served as a trustee and treasurer, and he currently hosts a weekly Friday afternoon programme. The show is well-known for its focus on 1960s music, a subject for which he has become a local authority. To mark the occasion, he was presented with a long-service certificate and received audio tributes from fellow broadcasters, including Hospital Broadcasting Association patron Alan Dedicoat.

item.title: Police appeal for witnesses following King's Lynn upskirting incident
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Police appeal for witnesses following King's Lynn upskirting incident
Norfolk Police are appealing for information after an upskirting incident in King’s Lynn on Wednesday. At approximately 11:55am, a man reportedly took a photograph underneath a teenage girl’s skirt on Gaywood Road, between Archdale Street and Loke Road.
The suspect is described as a white man in his late 40s or early 50s, standing around 5ft 7ins tall with a large build, tanned skin, and no facial hair or tattoos. He was wearing a dark blue-grey sweater and dark trousers. Officers are asking anyone who witnessed the event or has relevant information to contact them via the police website or by calling 101, quoting crime reference number 36/72074/26.

item.title: New children’s roleplay centre opens in King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
New children’s roleplay centre opens in King’s Lynn
A new roleplay centre and café has opened in King’s Lynn town centre today. Located on Purfleet Street in the former Rusty Krab premises, Roleplay King’s Lynn features three age-specific zones for children up to the age of 15. Facilities include a soft play area for toddlers, a miniature town for younger children, and a gaming den for older siblings.
The business, established by a local family, also includes a café serving speciality drinks and homemade snacks. The centre is open seven days a week, offering three 90-minute sessions daily. The team is also inviting schools and support groups to arrange exclusive bookings to provide a welcoming environment for children with special educational needs and disabilities.

item.title: Tributes paid to former Queen Elizabeth Hospital surgeon Graham Thompson
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Tributes paid to former Queen Elizabeth Hospital surgeon Graham Thompson
Tributes have been paid to Graham Thompson, a former surgeon at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn, who has died at the age of 96. Mr Thompson, who passed away on Wednesday, September 9, began his career in the Royal Navy before working in Wisbech and later moving to the QEH. He retired in 1994 but remained active in the medical community, establishing a walking group for retired consultants. His family described him as a remarkable man who transformed many lives during his career. A funeral service will be held at the West Suffolk Crematorium in Risby on Wednesday, October 7, at 12.30pm.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn man fined following Tower Gardens incident
A 38-year-old man has been fined after refusing to leave Tower Gardens in King’s Lynn. On July 3, police encountered Aleksandr Los, of Guanock Place, surrounded by beer cans and unable to stand properly. Officers reported that Mr Los refused to engage with them and shouted and swore in Romanian.
He was subsequently arrested for being drunk and disorderly. During a hearing at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Mr Los pleaded guilty to the charge. He told the court that he has since stopped drinking. The bench ordered him to pay a total of £271, consisting of a £133 fine, a £53 victim surcharge, and £85 in court costs.

item.title: Concerns raised over Queen Elizabeth Hospital services and new build delays
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Concerns raised over Queen Elizabeth Hospital services and new build delays
North West Norfolk MP James Wild has criticised the recent Queen Elizabeth Hospital Annual Members’ Meeting, describing it as a missed opportunity to reassure the public. Mr Wild stated that officials failed to guarantee the future of key services, including A&E, ICU, and maternity care, amid ongoing discussions regarding a clinical strategy review.
The meeting also revealed that the completion date for the new hospital has been pushed back to 2033. Mr Wild has written to the Health Secretary to urge that the previously promised 2032 deadline be maintained. Proposals for the clinical review are expected to go before the group board at the end of October, with a scrutiny session by Norfolk County Council scheduled for November.
